dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) targeting a Windows environment; Spanish-language identifiers, backslash path separators in COPY statements, MySQL SQL generation for data migration

purpose.domain_detail: Argentine retail/commerce ERP system data migration — exports legacy COBOL flat-file data to MySQL XML/SQL format covering articles, clients, suppliers, sales, purchases, payments, cheques, accounts, stock movements, etc.
purpose.summary: This batch program (MIGRACION-XML) reads data from a large set of legacy COBOL indexed/sequential files and generates MySQL INSERT/TRUNCATE SQL statements to migrate the data into a relational database. It covers virtually all business entities of an Argentine retail ERP: articles, clients, suppliers, sales, purchases, payments, cheques, accounts, stock, price lists, and audit tables. The program writes output SQL files in chunks controlled by a record counter.

notable_features: 164 COPY statements for file control and data structures
Generates MySQL SQL (INSERT/TRUNCATE) as text output
PIC X(5000) output record for SQL strings
548 PERFORM calls, zero GOTO — structured programming
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Chunked SQL file output with VAR-NUM-ARCHIVO counter
Covers ~50+ business tables including audit tables
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 5236 lines. Dialect is inferred as GnuCOBOL on Windows based on backslash COPY paths and absence of mainframe/MF-specific syntax. Could also be Micro Focus on Windows but GnuCOBOL is more likely given the open-source Argentine ERP context. The .FCN/.FSC/.TXE/.CPY copybook extensions are non-standard and specific to this application.
